recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow active-source correction in the same datatypes category wording family covered by FHIR-5232, and no additional related Jira decisions are needed.
issue_request: FHIR-5232 was a Published/Persuasive Jan 2015 ballot comment asking MnM to clarify the datatypes introduction because the old sentence could read as three categories: simple/primitive, imported from XML schema, and complex types.
initial_application: The original ambiguity was already removed by commit 8778bd12c1463e489868f342bb4b938870bc34fc, which rewrote the old sentence in source/datatypes.html to describe simple/primitive types as single elements. Later reorganizations replaced the two-category sentence with a list; commit 4652397b3f33fa5641bf58d760a47b3084417e2a changed the list from four to five categories but left a stale reference to categories 1 and 2.
additional_context: source/datatypes.html is in current build scope via source/fhir.ini's [type-pages] default mapping to datatypes. The current list places primitive datatypes at category 2 and general-purpose complex datatypes at category 3, so the follow-on sentence needed to name those categories. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Changed source/datatypes.html to say the page describes the primitive and general-purpose complex datatypes, categories 2 and 3.
source_changes: source/datatypes.html: updated the introductory page-scope sentence from general-purpose datatypes categories 1 and 2 to primitive and general-purpose complex datatypes categories 2 and 3.
